analyst_view.overall: Early view: Bremen (6th) and Leverkusen (5th) are one point apart in the race for Europe. Daniel Thioune's Bremen lean on an in-form Niclas Füllkrug but are without Mitchell Weiser (thigh) for an unknown period, while Carles Martinez's Leverkusen have leaked goals in the league and host Besiktas in the Europa League on the Thursday before this Sunday evening game.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals. I lean slightly higher: Leverkusen have conceded 17 in 9 league games, including 3-0 at Hoffenheim and 4-2 at home to Stuttgart, and Bremen's games have been open too (17 scored, 15 conceded). Füllkrug scored in seven league games in a row before the break.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners. Leverkusen create lots of attacks, but Bremen lose a key crosser on the right if Weiser is still out. Nothing points clearly either way yet.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards. A home game with European places at stake should be competitive, but neither side has a notable discipline problem in what I found. I stay with the number until the referee is named.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.2 shots. I lean a little higher: Leverkusen lead the Europa League for shots and xG, and their games this autumn have been open at both ends. Rotation after the Thursday game against Besiktas is the main risk to this.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 shots on target. That already fits two attacking sides, and Moussa Diaby's return from his thigh injury (one report expects him back after the November break) is still to be confirmed. I stay with the number for now.
